idea: When to replace old plumbing pipes
title: Internal Corrosion Signs in Galvanized Pipes
description: Galvanized steel pipes corrode from the inside out through a process called tuberculation. Over decades, rust and mineral deposits accumulate along the inner pipe walls, drastically restricting internal diameter. While the exterior of the pipe may still look structural and intact, internal tuberculation starves fixtures of water volume and flow rate. Pressure loss across multiple fixtures in older systems often indicates advanced internal scaling rather than a simple valve issue. When internal cross-sectional area is heavily choked by rust, localized cleaning is ineffective and total pipe replacement becomes necessary. What pipe material supplies your property?
image_prompt: Photorealistic educational studio cutaway view of an aged 3/4-inch galvanized steel water pipe section. The cross-sectional slice clearly shows severe internal rust scaling and thick orange-brown mineral tuberculation heavily clogging the inside diameter of the pipe, leaving only a tiny central opening for water. The outer metal wall remains grey and solid, demonstrating internal corrosion. The pipe is centered vertically on a clean neutral background. Professional directional studio lighting highlights the texture of the internal rust. Vertical 9:16 portrait composition, sharp focus, clean space at top and bottom for visual balance. No text, no logos, no watermarks, no diagrams, realistic plumbing details.
visual_story: The visual uses a clear physical cutaway of an old galvanized supply pipe to reveal what cannot be seen from the outside. The viewer observes how severe internal rust scaling (tuberculation) dramatically chokes the water channel while the exterior wall appears intact. This directly supports the lesson by demonstrating why low water volume in aging steel plumbing systems requires pipe replacement rather than superficial valve adjustments.

on_image_text.hook: Galvanized Pipes Corrode from the Inside Out
on_image_text.explanation: Internal rust buildup (tuberculation) shrinks water volume long before the pipe develops an external leak.
on_image_text.takeaway: Persistent low flow in old steel pipes signals internal choking—plan for pipe replacement.
